attribution_constraint: Do not claim a unique causal source unless the experiment actually isolates it. Evidence may be reported as consistent with a factor; it may not be reported as the cause. The system under test is the whole seam: Alpha -> resident -> stock Omega.

derived_analysis.exit_code_3_meaning: exit 3 is the controller's terminal state when the episode provider budget is consumed. Most two-turn runs carry termination_reason=responded alongside it, so exit 3 is the expected end of a fully spent two-turn budget, not a harness failure.
derived_analysis.why_not_the_v2_classifier: The v2 classifier treats any run whose episode-call count is not exactly 1 as infrastructure, which is correct for the one-turn v2 architecture but mislabels every two-turn V3-A run. analyze_v3a generalises the same causal chain from "exactly one episode call" to "within the run's permitted turn budget" and changes nothing else. The v2 classifier and every v2 artifact are untouched.

statistical_limitation.consequence: No representation effect and no scheduling effect is claimed. Under the frozen interpretation matrix several branches fire in contradictory directions, which is exactly the situation in which the non-attribution constraint forbids naming a cause. Establishing any such effect requires repeats, which this tranche did not preregister.
statistical_limitation.finding: Transitions occur in BOTH directions for the same manipulation: A1/R1 goes PASS->FAIL from one turn to two while A2/R1 goes FAIL->PASS, and R3 flips A1 PASS->FAIL at one turn but FAIL->PASS at two. With a single run per cell these are not separable from run-to-run variability.
